content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef, boiled or baked potatoes, and a variety of vegetables such as carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale). It is prepared without sauces, preserving the natural flavors of the ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is a rich source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than non‑heme iron.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables and are high in vitamin C and potassium.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound with antioxidant properties.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables are packed with folate, essential for cell division.
The absence of sauce reduces added sugars and sodium.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete animal protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Bone health support
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K found in leafy greens help strengthen bones.

items.title: Blood pressure regulation
items.content: Potassium in potatoes assists in maintaining proper fluid balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C in potatoes and carotenoids in carrots protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: The combination of vitamins A, C and iron enhances immune function.

items.title: Excessive red meat intake
items.content: Consuming large amounts of beef may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease if not balanced with plant foods.

items.title: Vegetable allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to broccoli or leafy greens.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: While the dish itself is low in sodium, added salt during cooking can raise the level.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Beef should be cooked thoroughly to avoid salmonella or other bacterial infections.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the beef thinly, cutting potatoes into cubes or wedges, and lightly steaming or sautéing the vegetables. Fresh herbs such as parsley or dill can be added for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before consuming.

beef-potatoes-and-vegetables-including-c.title: Beef with Potatoes and Vegetables in Tomato Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of tender beef, boiled or roasted potatoes, and a mix of vegetables – carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale). All ingredients are simmered in a flavorful tomato‑based sauce, making the meal hearty and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef provides highly bioavailable iron, especially when paired with vitamin C from tomatoes.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables and retain most nutrients when steamed or baked.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound with documented anti‑cancer properties.
Dark‑green leafy greens are rich in lutein and zeaxanthin, which support eye health.
Tomato sauce made from ripe tomatoes is a great source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Beef is high in complete protein and creatine, which aid muscle growth and recovery.

items.title: Blood‑sugar stability
items.content: Fiber from potatoes and vegetables slows glucose absorption, helping maintain steady blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and broccoli enhances the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene and sulforaphane protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Fatty cuts of beef can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: Those prone to kidney stones should limit high‑oxalate greens such as spinach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear beef cubes until browned, then add diced potatoes, carrots, broccoli, and leafy greens. Pour tomato sauce over the mixture and simmer 30–40 minutes until tender. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months after cooling.

beef-prepackaged-or-deli-luncheon-meat-r.title: Beef, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat, reduced sodium

content.title: About
content.content: Beef prepackaged deli luncheon meat is cooked or smoked beef sliced thinly and sealed in vacuum or plastic packs. The reduced‑sodium version (1018) contains about 0.5 g of salt per 100 g, allowing lower sodium intake without sacrificing flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef deli meat is a classic filling for sandwiches, salads, and snack platters.
Sodium reduction is achieved by using natural flavor enhancers, spices, and fermented ingredients.
Vacuum packaging extends shelf life up to 30 days without added preservatives.
The product can be served cold or gently warmed to enhance aroma.
In the US, code “1018” designates the “Reduced Sodium” category in food labeling.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids, making it an excellent source of complete protein.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain normal blood pressure and reduces kidney load.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support hemoglobin formation and immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low carbohydrate
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Nitrite content
items.content: Certain deli meats may contain small amounts of nitrites as preservatives.

items.title: Foodborne pathogens
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Depending on the cut, the product can contain up to 15 % fat, which should be considered in diet planning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the meat cold in sandwiches, sliced into salads, added to pasta, or lightly pan‑seared. It pairs well with mustard, fresh vegetables, and whole‑grain bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C in the original package. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. If frozen, store up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Nonfat Swiss cheese is a low‑fat version of the classic Swiss cheese that retains its characteristic holes and nutty flavor while containing virtually no fat. It is made from skimmed cow’s milk, offering the same protein and calcium content with far fewer calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Swiss cheese is famous for its “eyes,” which form from gas bubbles produced by bacteria during aging.
The nonfat version was developed to meet growing consumer demand for reduced‑fat dairy products.
Traditional Swiss cheese ages 3–6 months; the nonfat variety often has a shorter aging period to keep a softer texture.
It can be used in fondue, but the low‑fat version requires a longer melt time to avoid breaking apart.
In the United States, nonfat Swiss cheese is classified as a low‑fat cheese with less than 0.5 % fat.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Swiss cheese provides a high amount of calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Despite being fat‑free, it still delivers almost the same amount of high‑quality protein as regular Swiss cheese.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The negligible fat content makes it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial bacteria that may support gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although some lactose is removed during processing, the cheese still contains lactose and may cause symptoms in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Like most cheeses, nonfat Swiss can be relatively salty, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Those allergic to casein or whey proteins should avoid this cheese.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use nonfat Swiss cheese in sandwiches, salads, casseroles, or as a topping for omelets. It can be sliced thin, grated, or melted into sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. It stays fresh for 2‑3 weeks. Discard if mold appears or if it develops an off‑odor.

chocolate-beverage-powder-dry-mix-not-re.title: Chocolate beverage powder, dry mix, not reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate beverage powder is a dry mix designed for preparing a hot or cold chocolate drink by adding water or milk. It contains cocoa mass, sugar, dry milk and flavorings. No pre‑reconstitution is needed; it simply dissolves in the liquid.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The powder is easy to store and transport because it does not require refrigeration.
Formulations often include emulsifiers that keep the drink smooth without settling.
Chocolate powders are popular in schools and offices due to quick preparation.
In some countries the mix is used as a base for dessert sauces.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and carbohydrates provide a rapid source of energy, useful during periods of high mental activity.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Dry milk supplies calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa mass contains flavonoids that have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain milk proteins and soy emulsifiers, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Some blends contain caffeine, which should be considered by caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix 1–2 tablespoons of powder with 200–250 ml of hot or cold water/milk, stir until smooth. Optional additions include cream, spices (cinnamon, vanilla) or extra sweeteners to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place with the package tightly sealed. For long‑term storage, keep in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and flavor loss.

content.title: About
content.content: Jam or jelly, sugar free (item 5057) is a fruit spread made from fresh berries or fruits and sweetened with sugar substitutes such as stevia or erythritol. It retains the natural fruit flavor while providing low calories and a low glycemic index, making it suitable for people monitoring blood sugar levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar‑free jams often use pectin derived from apples or citrus to achieve the right thickness.
Sugar substitutes keep the product sweet without raising blood glucose.
The product can be completely vegan when it does not contain gelatin.
Without sugar as a preservative, these jams can have a longer shelf life thanks to modern packaging.
Flavor ranges from bright tart to gently sweet depending on the fruit blend and sweetener used.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: The fruits used provide vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Absence of sugar makes the spread safe for diabetics and low‑carb diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Natural pectin acts as a soluble fiber, promoting healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Reduced calorie content
items.content: Sugar substitutes add minimal calories, aiding energy balance.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Depending on the fruit base, the jam can supply B‑vitamins, potassium and magnesium.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to specific berries or fruits used in the product.

items.title: Sensitivity to sugar substitutes
items.content: Polyol sweeteners like erythritol can cause gastrointestinal discomfort if consumed in large amounts.

items.title: High pectin content
items.content: Large amounts of pectin may interfere with the absorption of certain minerals such as iron and zinc.

items.title: Preservative additives
items.content: Some versions may contain small amounts of preservatives; people with sensitivities should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sugar‑free jam can be spread on bread, toast, crackers, used as a filling for pancakes, stirred into yogurt or cottage cheese, or incorporated into recipes that call for a sweet fruit note without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep the jam refrigerated in a tightly sealed jar. Unopened jars can be stored in a cool, dry place until the printed expiration date. Discard the product if it develops an off‑smell, mold, or unusual color.

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced sodium ketchup is a tomato‑based sauce made from ripe tomatoes, vinegar, sugar and spices, but with a lower amount of added salt (about 0.3 g per 100 g). It retains the classic sweet‑tangy flavor of regular ketchup while being suitable for those watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ketchup originated in the United States in the 19th century as a tomato sauce served with seafood.
The reduced‑salt formulation relies on natural flavor enhancers and more concentrated tomato paste.
In several countries the product is classified as a “dietary food” due to its lower sodium content.
Tomatoes used are often grown without synthetic fertilizers, enhancing their nutritional profile.
Ketchup serves as a base for barbecue sauces, marinades, and salad dressings.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps control blood pressure and lessens the burden on the kidneys.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and improves iron absorption from plant foods.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Vinegar stimulates gastric juice production, promoting better digestion.

items.title: Lower calorie taste
items.content: Compared with regular ketchup, the reduced‑salt version often contains slightly fewer calories due to modest sugar reduction.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even with less salt, the sauce may contain notable amounts of sugar, which diabetics should monitor.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or added spices.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Preservatives used to extend shelf life may not be suitable for people sensitive to them.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced sodium ketchup works as a condiment for fries, burgers, hot dogs, and as an ingredient in sauces, marinades, and salad dressings. Use it sparingly to keep the overall sodium level of your dish in check.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the ketchup in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3–4 weeks. Discard if you notice changes in color, odor, or any mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Non-dairy milk NFS (203) is a lactose‑free beverage made from a blend of plant‑based ingredients such as oats, rice, or nuts. It has a smooth, creamy taste and is suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance. The product is commonly used in coffee, cereals, baking, and as a cow‑milk substitute.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS (203) is formulated with low sugar content, making it diet‑friendly.
The blend includes plant proteins that provide a complete amino‑acid profile.
It is fortified with calcium, vitamin D and B12 to match the nutritional profile of dairy milk.
Plant‑based milk has a lower carbon footprint than animal milk.
NFS (203) undergoes homogenization to prevent separation.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fortified with vitamin D and B12, it supports bone health and the nervous system.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Contains mainly polyunsaturated fats, which are heart‑healthy.

items.title: Digestive friendly
items.content: Absence of lactose makes it safe for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Fortification provides calcium to help maintain strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Plant antioxidants help combat free radicals.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: The product may contain nuts, soy or oats, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Some varieties contain added sugar; choose unsweetened versions if monitoring calorie intake.

items.title: Lower protein compared to cow's milk
items.content: While it provides plant protein, the amount is usually lower than that of dairy milk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Non-dairy milk NFS (203) can be enjoyed on its own, added to coffee, tea, smoothies, cereals, baked goods, and sauces. It pairs well with fruits, berries, and granola.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1 °C–4 °C. After opening, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as texture may change.

nutritional-powder-mix-sugar-free-slim-f.title: Nutritional powder mix, sugar free (Slim Fast)

content.title: About
content.content: Slim Fast sugar‑free nutritional powder mix is designed for quick preparation of low‑calorie drinks, helps maintain satiety and supports weight management. The powder provides protein, vitamins and minerals without added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Slim Fast was first launched in the 1970s as part of a weight‑control program.
The powder dissolves easily in water or milk, creating a smooth beverage.
Several flavors are available, including vanilla, chocolate and strawberry.
Athletes and active individuals often use it for rapid nutrient replenishment.
The mix is gluten‑free and suitable for most diets, except those avoiding artificial sweeteners.

items.title: Supports satiety
items.content: High protein and fiber content helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B6 and B12 aid normal metabolism and energy production.

items.title: Mineral complex
items.content: Includes calcium, magnesium and iron, essential for bones and blood formation.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: No added sugar makes it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: Quick to prepare, facilitating adherence to a regular eating schedule.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some versions contain whey protein, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Contains sucralose or aspartame, which may not be suitable for sensitive individuals.

items.title: Vitamin excess
items.content: Overconsumption could lead to exceeding recommended daily intakes of certain vitamins.

items.title: Not a meal replacement
items.content: Intended as a supplement, not as the sole source of nutrition.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix one scoop (about 30 g) of powder with 250 ml of water, milk or a plant‑based beverage, shake well. For extra flavor and texture, add fruit, berries or nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed to prevent moisture ingress.

content.title: About
content.content: Topping from vegetable pizza is a blend of roasted vegetables used as a pizza topping. Typical ingredients include tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, olives, and sometimes artichokes. The vegetables add bright flavor, aroma, and increased nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetable toppings are often sautéed in olive oil to enhance their aroma.
Combining different vegetables provides a wide range of vitamins and minerals in one serving.
Traditional Italian pizza uses fresh, seasonal vegetables rather than canned ones.
A vegetable topping can be vegan and gluten‑free when no cheese is added.
Roasting vegetables until lightly caramelized brings out their natural sweetness.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and C
items.content: Tomatoes, bell peppers, and spinach are high in vitamins A and C, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables provide fiber that promotes healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Compared with meat toppings, vegetable versions are generally lower in calories, useful for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Lycopene in tomatoes and quercetin in onions help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium found in vegetables aids in maintaining normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy to individual vegetables
items.content: Some people may be allergic to tomatoes, peppers, or mushrooms.

items.title: Sodium content in ready‑made mixes
items.content: Commercial mixes can be salted; always check the label.

items.title: Potential pesticide residues
items.content: If vegetables are not thoroughly washed, chemical residues may remain.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Spread the vegetable pizza topping evenly over the dough before baking, add it to a finished pizza as a fresh garnish, use it in wraps, pasta, or as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared vegetable topping in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Before use, check for any off‑smells or spoilage.
